The problem is that this code directly reads `TASKS_FILE` without first checking whether the file exists. When the tasks file is missing, `TASKS_FILE.read_text()` raises an error, causing the whole hand‑off logic to crash. Moreover, the test suite now includes two new tests I just appended to `tests/test_ralph_helpers.py`:

1. `test_unfinished_work_remains_true_when_tasks_file_missing` – expects `unfinished_work_remains()` to return `True` when the tasks file does not exist.
2. `test_unfinished_work_remains_tracks_unchecked_boxes` – expects `unfinished_work_remains()` to return `True` when there is at least one unchecked task (`- [ ]`) and `False` when all tasks are checked (`- [x]`).

These tests imply that the repository wants a dedicated helper `unfinished_work_remains()` that encapsulates exactly the logic currently embedded in `rate_limit_handoff`. By extracting this logic into its own function, I can both satisfy the new tests and make `rate_limit_handoff` safer (it will call the helper instead of directly accessing the file).

    if not TASKS_FILE.is_file():
